analysis:
Examined the workflow excerpt, all five added changelogs and their metadata, and the build-documentation patch against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. No concrete regression is established in this scope. In .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml:1205-1214, Darkbloom-named runners without a cache URL disable Actions caching; restore/save steps at 1223 and 1265 honor that flag. Restored .git validation at 1063-1088 and 1232-1257 adds rejection of symlinks, hooks and selected executable/include configuration before repository validation. This improves existing cache handling, but is not proof that arbitrary cached Git configuration is inert. Checkout retains persist-credentials:false. The existing gate at 1398-1428 requires selected lanes and CI-plan checks to succeed.
Documentation describes newly routed build, GPU and unsigned desktop-package jobs, per-lane approval/fallback behavior, and test-only MLX buffer-cache limits. These limits are distinct from T-041's encrypted production prefix cache; no supplied change alters its cryptography, scope, TTL or donation policy. No direct serving-authorization, attestation, plaintext transport, billing or privileged-helper change is visible.
Integration must inspect provider-plan.yml routing/approval validation, desktop.yml dispatch and artifact handling, and provider-ci-build/provider-release-build cache provenance and consumption. Newly routed build products make isolation from adversarial provider hosts relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054; the supplied material does not establish host protections, cache writer isolation or promotion into signed releases. Also reconcile cache gating across other workflows/composites and inspect the actual BoundedBufferCache/benchmark changes rather than relying on documentation claims. These are coverage limits and material integration questions, not supported vulnerabilities.
